did_you_know.text: Did you know? According to the account, Darius the Mede received the kingdom when he was sixty-two years old.
Did you know? Darius appointed 120 satraps throughout the kingdom—administrative officials stationed across the empire.
Did you know? Over the 120 satraps, he appointed three administrators, one of whom was Daniel. Their role was to supervise the satraps so that the king would not suffer loss.
Did you know? Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators because of his exceptional spirit, so much so that Darius considered placing him over the entire kingdom.
Did you know? Daniel’s enemies could find no grounds for accusation or corruption in his royal affairs, because he was trustworthy and no negligence was found in him.
Did you know? After Daniel learned about the decree, he continued to pray three times a day, with the windows of his upper room open toward Jerusalem.

Did you know? After Daniel was thrown into the lions’ den, a stone was placed over its opening, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and the rings of his officials, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.

Did you know? Daniel was brought out of the den without a single injury, and the account explains that this was because he trusted in his God. Daniel also said that God had sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths.
Did you know? In his proclamation, Darius describes Daniel’s God as the living God, whose kingdom will never be destroyed and whose rule will endure to the end.
Did you know? The chapter ends by saying that Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
